selection_reasoning: These three tasks form a coherent exploration and interaction sequence. The player must first locate a trapped_chest (which will be placed inside a structure made with dark_oak_stairs), then mine the dark_oak_stairs that form part of the structure to access a hidden area behind them, where the orange_banner is concealed. This creates a natural multi-hop dependency: finding the chest reveals the structure, mining the stairs opens a path, and the banner is the final discovery. All tasks are observable and verifiable without deep Minecraft crafting knowledge.

edges.reason: The trapped_chest is a landmark identifying the structure; its location guides the player to the dark_oak_stairs that must be mined
Mining the dark_oak_stairs removes the wall blocking access to the hidden room containing the orange_banner

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The trapped chest is at spawn-relative (1, 1, 6) inside the front room of the structure. The player must approach within 8 blocks and face toward it, modeling 'player can see the trapped chest'. Max distance of 8 is generous since the player spawns ~6 blocks away and must walk forward slightly. Facing tolerance of 60° ensures the player is actually looking at the chest.

Uses inventory_has because this is a mine task — when dark oak stairs are mined with an axe, they drop as items that enter the player's inventory. The player needs to mine at least 1 dark_oak_stairs block from the 9×3 wall (27 total blocks) to begin creating an opening. We require min_count=1 since even a single mined stair confirms the player has started breaking through the barrier. The item ID for the drop is 'dark_oak_stairs'.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The orange banner is at spawn-relative (1, 1, 12) in the hidden back room behind the dark oak stairs wall. The player must navigate through the mined opening in the stairs wall and approach within 5 blocks while facing the banner. Max distance of 5 ensures the player has actually passed through the wall (the wall is at Z=9, banner at Z=12, so from the front room the minimum distance would be >5 through the solid wall). Facing tolerance of 60° ensures the player is looking at the banner.

scene_description: A stone brick structure with two rooms separated by a dark oak stairs wall. The front room contains a trapped chest as a landmark. The back room, hidden behind the dark oak stairs wall, contains an orange banner flanked by torches. The player must find the trapped chest, mine through the dark oak stairs barrier with the provided diamond axe, and discover the orange banner in the hidden room.
task_text: Enter the stone brick structure and find the trapped chest. Then use the diamond axe to mine through the dark oak stairs wall behind the chest. Discover the orange banner hidden in the room behind the stairs.
design_notes: Structure spans ~-4 to ~6 on X, ~4 to ~13 on Z. Front room (Z=5-8) has the trapped chest at ~1,~1,~6. Dark oak stairs wall at Z=9 spans X=-3 to 5, Y=1-3. Hidden back room (Z=10-12) has the orange banner at ~1,~1,~12 with torches at ~0 and ~2. Player spawns facing the entrance (Z=4 front wall with opening from X=-1 to X=3). Diamond axe provided for mining stairs. Air fill at start clears any natural vegetation.
